name: CompanyEnrich
description: Live B2B company and people data for AI agents. Enrich a company by domain, name, or social profile, search companies and people, find similar companies, and look up a person from an email address.
author: CompanyEnrich

tools.name: enrich_company
tools.description: Enriches a company by domain. Costs 1 credit per successful enrichment. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company. A company that cannot be found costs nothing.

domain.description: The domain name of the company to enrich, for example example.com.

expand.description: Extra company data to include. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company.

waitForEnrichment.description: Whether to wait for on-demand enrichment when the company is not stored yet. Defaults to true. Set false to return only stored data right away; a miss then schedules enrichment in the background.

tools.name: get_company_by_id
tools.description: Retrieves a stored company by CompanyEnrich company ID. Costs 1 credit per company returned. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company. A company that cannot be found costs nothing.

expand.description: Extra company data to include. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company.

tools.name: enrich_company_by_properties
tools.description: Resolves and enriches a company from identifying properties such as its name or a social profile URL. When several properties are given, all of them must match. Prefer enrich_company when the domain is known. Costs 1 credit when a company is returned or when the properties cannot be resolved to a company domain. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company.

expand.description: Extra company data to include. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company.

tools.name: get_company_workforce
tools.description: Returns the current employee count, department headcounts and the latest 12 months of workforce history for one company, looked up by CompanyEnrich company ID or domain. Pass `nextCursor` from the response as `cursor`, with the same company, to get the preceding 12 months. Costs 1 credit per successful page. Cursors expire after 30 minutes.

id.description: CompanyEnrich company ID. Provide either id or domain.

domain.description: Company domain. Provide either id or domain.

cursor.description: `nextCursor` from a previous workforce response or from a company's workforce expansion. Omit for the latest 12 months.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Searches companies in one of three ways: by filters alone, by a natural-language `semantic` query, or by `lookalike` seed domains (companies similar to the ones given). Filters can be combined with either; semantic and lookalike cannot be combined. A semantic query infers filters such as location, size and funding by default and reports them in `interpretation`. Costs per returned company: 1 credit for a filter search, 2 for semantic, 5 for lookalike; an empty result costs one result's price. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company. Each value filter is an object: `in` matches any listed value, `notIn` excludes matches, and `all` (keywords, technologies, naicsCodes and categories only) requires every listed value. Results are paged with a cursor: pass `nextCursor` from the previous response as `cursor` and keep the rest of the query the same. Cursors expire after 24 hours.

query.description: Text matched against company names, keywords and domain prefixes.

reportedEmployees.description: Employee count ranges as reported by external sources.

period.description: Period to measure growth over: m6, y1 or y2.

department.description: Department to measure. Use overall for the whole company.

min.description: Minimum growth ratio, inclusive. 0.15 is 15% growth; negative values are declines.

workforceSize.description: Headcount ranges, one entry per department.

department.description: Department to count. Use overall for the whole company.

naicsCodes.description: NAICS codes as strings of 2 to 6 digits, for example "5112".

require.description: Data the company must have, for example a LinkedIn profile.

semantic.description: Natural-language company search. Cannot be combined with lookalike.

query.description: Natural-language description of the companies to find, for example "saas companies in Turkey".

weight.description: Semantic relevance weight from 0 to 1. Larger values favor semantic similarity.

autoFilter.description: Whether to infer filters such as location, size and funding from the query. Defaults to true. The response `interpretation` reports what was inferred.

lookalike.description: Finds companies similar to seed companies. Cannot be combined with semantic.

domains.description: Seed company domains to find lookalikes for. Up to 10.

weight.description: Ranking weight from -1 to 1. Larger values favor more similar companies.

expand.description: Extra company data to include. Each expansion (financial, keywords, naicsCodes, technologies, workforce) adds 1 credit per returned company.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100.

cursor.description: `nextCursor` from the previous response. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: count_companies
tools.description: Counts the companies a search_companies query would match, without returning them. Free; no credits deducted. Use it to size or check a query before running the paid search. Takes the same `filter`, `semantic` and `lookalike` arguments as search_companies. Returns `count`, the matches your plan can access, and `total`, all matches. A semantic query also returns `interpretation`, the filters inferred from it.

tools.name: get_person_by_id
tools.description: Retrieves a stored person by CompanyEnrich person ID. Costs 2 credits per person returned. Expansions: education adds 1 credit per returned person; company adds 1 credit per unique company whose profile is included. A person that cannot be found costs nothing.

expand.description: Extra person data to include. Expansions: education adds 1 credit per returned person; company adds 1 credit per unique company whose profile is included.

tools.name: lookup_person_by_email
tools.description: Identifies a person from an email address. The API resolves the company from the email domain and matches the person by common address patterns. Costs 5 credits when a person is returned. Expansions: education adds 1 credit per returned person; company adds 1 credit per unique company whose profile is included. No match costs nothing.

email.description: The email address of the person to look up.

expand.description: Extra person data to include. Expansions: education adds 1 credit per returned person; company adds 1 credit per unique company whose profile is included.

tools.name: enrich_person_email
tools.description: Finds the work email address of a person on a company domain. The response `status` is found, not-found, unavailable or pending; `email` is present only when found, and a pending lookup is still running, so call again later. Costs 10 credits when it finds an email your account has not accessed before; every other outcome is free.

domain.description: Company domain to find the email on. It must belong to one of the person's companies. If omitted, the person's current companies are tried.

tools.name: search_people
tools.description: Searches people by person filters, a natural-language `semantic` query, and an optional `company` query that limits results to people whose current company matches. `company` takes the same filter, semantic and lookalike inputs as search_companies. A semantic query infers person filters and the kind of company to look in, and reports them in `interpretation`; it is rejected when nothing can be inferred. Top-level filters match current roles; use `filter.pastExperience` for previous jobs. Costs 2 credits per returned person; an empty result costs one result's price. Expansions: education adds 1 credit per returned person; company adds 1 credit per unique company whose profile is included. Each value filter is an object: `in` matches any listed value, `notIn` excludes matches, and `all` (keywords, technologies, naicsCodes and categories only) requires every listed value. Results are paged with a cursor: pass `nextCursor` from the previous response as `cursor` and keep the rest of the query the same. Cursors expire after 24 hours.

companyLinkedinHandle.description: LinkedIn handles or URLs of current companies.

department.description: Current departments. A root department includes its sub-departments.

position.description: Phrases matched against current job titles.

currentCompanyStartDate.description: When the person joined their current company.

currentPositionStartDate.description: When the person started their current position.

institutionLinkedinHandle.description: LinkedIn handles or URLs of schools.

pastExperience.description: Finds people by a previous job. All rules must match the same past role, and people still at an included company are left out.
